$comment: Resolutions for the 15 dot points that reference/syllabus/year12_syllabus_seed.json
marks verified:false. Those items contain the token UNRESOLVED because the NESA
content pages render glossary-linked terms as lazy-loaded links: a server-side
fetch receives the literal string 'Loading' in their place, which produces text
that reads as valid English but is factually wrong.
Each exactText below was read from the live page in a real browser, where the
terms hydrate correctly, and is copied verbatim. The live page is the authority.
This file lives in web/ rather than being patched into the seed because
reference/ is read-only source material. The seed loader applies these on read.
Two of the informed guesses recorded in SYLLABUS_VERIFICATION.md were wrong and
are corrected here: pwa.2.14 is Object-Relational Mapping (ORM), not NoSQL; and
proj.3.8 needed two terms, not one.
method: Read in a browser with JavaScript enabled, so glossary terms hydrate.

pwa.1.2.exactText: Investigate and practise how data is transferred on the internet

pwa.1.3.exactText: Investigate and describe the function of web protocols and their ports

pwa.1.5.exactText: Investigate the effect of big data on web architecture

pwa.2.1.exactText: Investigate and explain the role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) in the development of applications for the web

pwa.2.9.exactText: Research, experiment with and evaluate the prevalence and use of web content management systems (CMS)

pwa.2.12.exactText: Develop a web application using an appropriate scripting language with shell scripts to make files and directories, and searching for text in a text file
pwa.2.12.note: The seed is short of more than the glossary term here: it ends at 'searching for text', and the live page ends 'searching for text in a text file'. Substituting the term alone would still leave the wording wrong.

pwa.2.14.note: SYLLABUS_VERIFICATION.md guessed NoSQL. That guess was wrong.

auto.1.2.exactText: Distinguish between artificial intelligence (AI) and ML

auto.1.4.exactText: Investigate common applications of key ML algorithms

auto.2.1.exactText: Design, develop and apply ML regression models using an OOP to predict numeric values

proj.3.5.exactText: Demonstrate the use of programmed data backup

proj.3.8.exactText: Propose an additional innovative solution using a prototype and user interface (UI) design
proj.3.8.note: Two glossary terms in one dot point, as SYLLABUS_VERIFICATION.md warned.

proj.4.1.exactText: Apply methodologies to test and evaluate code
